title: Benchmarking experiments: warmup, seeds, and reproducibility plan
body:
Purpose
This note records a practical, reproducible methodology for running throughput benchmark experiments against the serving runtime with explicit warmup behavior, fixed seeds, and noise mitigation. The goal: produce repeatable runs (within acceptance bounds), capture the root causes of variance, and make benchmarking metadata machine-readable so runs can be audited later.

Scope
- Focus: production-style text generation workloads (decoder-only transformer models) across GPU-backed dedicated nodes.
- Not in scope: model training or multi-node distributed training benchmarks.

Principles
1) Make each run deterministic at the experiment level: versioned code, pinned container images, pinned drivers, and a reproducible load profile.
2) Separate warmup from measurement. Clear boundaries reduce conflation of compilation/warm caches with steady-state throughput.
3) Capture rich telemetry: both application-level (tokens/sec, latencies by percentile) and infra-level (GPU SM%, PCIe, host CPU).
4) Run enough repetitions to quantify variance; use simple statistical tests to detect regressions.

Experiment topology and metadata to record (always)
- git_commit: git rev-parse --short HEAD
- container_image: e.g. ghcr.io/redwood-inference/runtime:2025-01-10-rc3
- driver: NVIDIA 545.60.11, CUDA 12.2
- kernel: Linux 6.1.XX
- model: name + model_sha256 (file digest)
- model_compile_cache_path: /var/lib/redwood/model_cache/<hash>
- build_flags: list (e.g. USE_FAST_ATTENTION=1)
- batcher_config_id: numeric id or filename
- loadgen_config_id: filename (see template below)
- host_clock: date --iso-8601=seconds
- notes: free text

Load generator config (recommended fields)
- request_type: streaming|nonstreaming
- seq_length_distribution: (mean, std, sample list) or production trace id
- prompt_length_tokens: int or distribution
- tokens_per_completion_target: typical number tokens generated per request
- concurrency_profile: constant|poisson|sawtooth
- warmup_profile: see section below
- seed: int (fixed for the run)
- target_duration_seconds: int (duration of MEASUREMENT window)
- clients: number of parallel client processes

Warmup strategy (practical recipe)
We observed two distinct warmup effects: (A) binary/kernel autoselection and JIT/kernels warm compilation that occurs on first requests, and (B) runtime warm caches (KV cache priming, CUDA context, cuBLAS heuristics). Our goal is to ensure measurement starts after (A) and is stable wrt (B).

Recommended multi-stage warmup (durations are starting recommendations; tune per-model):
1) Cold-cold priming (quick compilation pass): 2 minutes of single-request sequential runs at short sequence length (<= 32 tokens). Purpose: force lazy kernel selection, model deserialization, initial memory allocation.
2) Parallel ramp (compilation + cache fill): 4 minutes using target concurrency but short sequences (seq <= 64). This allows per-stream compilation in parallel paths but with short total runtime.
3) Full-sequence KV warm: 6 minutes using target concurrency and target sequence lengths (or production distribution). Purpose: fill KV cache hotspots and thermalize GPU.
4) Stabilization hold: 2 minutes at target concurrency; collect telemetry but do not include in measurement.

After warmup: start measurement window for N seconds (target_duration_seconds). Always discard the first 30 seconds of the measurement window if traces show residual drift.

Notes on warmup sizing
- Small models/short sequences: reduce times proportionally.
- High quantization/auto-fallback paths: increase warmup to ensure fallback paths are exercised prior to measurement.
- If binary/kernel selection is nondeterministic across runs (observed on some driver versions), collect full trace during first cold run and pin the kernel cache directory into the model cache for subsequent runs.

Reproducibility checklist (run before measurement)
- [ ] confirm git_commit, container_image, and driver versions recorded
- [ ] set CPU governor to performance (sudo cpufreq-set -g performance)
- [ ] isolate benchmark process on reserved CPU cores (taskset/numactl) and pin interrupts off those cores (irqbalance rules)
- [ ] disable background services that cause periodic work (snapd, unattended-upgrades) or record expected cron windows
- [ ] set transparent hugepages to never: echo never > /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled
- [ ] export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and record mapping
- [ ] ensure model compile cache path is either empty (for cold run) or prepopulated and recorded (for warm runs)
- [ ] set environment variables that affect determinism: TF_CUDNN_USE_AUTOTUNE=0 (if applicable), or runtime-specific flags logged

Telemetry and tracing to capture
- Application: tokens/sec, requests/sec, p50/p90/p95/p99 latency for request-to-first-token and request-to-last-token, percent streamed vs batched paths
- Runtime: per-GPU SM util, GPU memory usage, GPU temperature, PCIe bandwidth, PCIe errors, host CPU usage per core, RSS/minor page faults
- Kernel-level: nvtx markers placed around model forward and KV cache handling; nsight-compute or Nsight Systems collection for one representative run; ROCm equivalents if needed
- OS-level: perf record for hot paths, top/dstat, iostat for NVMe if loading models from disk

Sizing runs and statistical approach
- Minimum repetitions: 7 independent runs (complete warmup + measurement). We prefer 10 when time allows. Treat each repetition as an independent sample.
- For each metric (throughput, p95 latency) compute mean and standard deviation across runs. Accept if coefficient of variation (std/mean) < 0.03 for throughput unless profiling proves otherwise.
- Use two-sided t-test for paired comparisons when distributions appear Gaussian and sample size >= 7. For non-normal distributions or small N, use Mann-Whitney U test. Report p-value and effect size (Cohen's d or rank-biserial).
- Always report confidence intervals (95%) for throughput and p95. For p99 consider using bootstrap resampling due to heavy tails.

Anchors and sanity checks
- Single-run telemetry should show no large drift in throughput across measurement window (>5% change across windows). If drift exists, increase stabilization hold or investigate thermal throttling.
- GPU clock throttling: check nvidia-smi --query-gpu=clocks.sm,clocks.gr,clocks.mem,temperature.gpu --format=csv -l 1 during runs.
- If host CPU becomes the bottleneck (CPU% > 70% on serving threads), scale clients or increase CPU allocation per job.

Handling randomness from load generator and model sampling
- For deterministic throughput tests, use greedy decoding or fixed seeds for sampling-based decoders. Record seed value under loadgen_config.
- For stochastic tests (sampling), treat generated sequence length variance as part of the workload; increase repetitions and report distribution of tokens/sec.

Example loadgen invocations (templates)
- k6-like synthetic: ./loadgen --config configs/benchmark-bert-64.json --seed 1234 --clients 16 --warmup 720 --measure 600 --out metadata.json
- custom python runner: python run_benchmark.py --model models/7B --clients 8 --seq-distr production_trace_202411 --seed 42 --warmup-stages warm1,warm2,warm3 --out run-2025-02-02.json

Common sources of irreproducibility and mitigations
- Kernel selection jitter: pin model compile cache and capture kernel selection artifacts.
- GPU driver upgrades: treat driver version changes as major experimental changes. Re-run baselines when drivers differ.
- Noisy co-tenants: run on dedicated nodes or use Dedicated capacity. If using shared machines, measure background noise using an idle sampler.
- System thermal throttling: observe temperature and use stabilization hold. If throttling occurs, replicate with deliberate cool-down between runs.

Profiling pass for regression triage (when variance or regression observed)
1) Re-run failing benchmark with NVTX markers enabled and collect Nsight Systems timeline.
2) Capture pprof/perf and GPU traces (nsys profile) for the first 2 minutes of measurement.
3) Dump per-request operator durations via runtime tracing to identify long tails.
4) Correlate with infra metrics (PCIe, CPU) to determine if slowdowns are compute, memory copy, or host-side queueing.

Run metadata format (machine-readable JSON blob to store alongside artifacts)
- run_id: uuid string
- start_time: timestamp
- git_commit: string
- container_image: string
- driver: string
- loadgen_config_id: string
- warmup_profile: string
- seed: int
- measurement_seconds: int
- raw_artifacts: [paths-to-nsight, nvtx, system-metrics]

Acceptance criteria for experimental runs in CI (if running nightly)
- baseline throughput must be within 5% of reference mean for the same commit and environment (n>=7).
- p95 latency must not increase by >10% unless accompanied by >=6% throughput improvement and an owner-approved tradeoff.
- If criteria fail, mark run as blocked and open a JIRA with attached artifacts.

Templates and quick checklist for on-call and SRE to run an ad-hoc regression check
- grab commit and container: export COMMIT=...; docker pull ...
- clear model cache or preserve it depending on test
- run warmup sequence (script provided): ./scripts/run_warmup.sh --config ... --seed 42
- start measurement: ./scripts/start_measurement.sh --run-id $RUNID
- collect artifacts: ./scripts/collect_artifacts.sh --out /tmp/artifacts/$RUNID
- upload artifacts to shared bucket and link into JIRA ticket

Known open items and follow-ups
- Build a small utility that automatically validates kernel cache parity across nodes (RLINF-842).
- Add a standardized JSON schema for loadgen configs and publish in repo.
- Investigate enabling deterministic kernel choices by saving and replaying cuBLAS heuristics (driver permitting).

Appendix: example short loadgen config (JSON snippet)
{
  "name": "prod-shortgen-8clients",
  "request_type": "nonstreaming",
  "seq_length_distribution": "production_trace_202412",
  "prompt_tokens": 32,
  "clients": 8,
  "seed": 12345,
  "warmup_stages": ["cold-priming:120", "parallel-ramp:240", "kv-warm:360"]
}

If you run this experiment, paste the run metadata here and ping #eng-serving-runtime with the run_id for quick review.

Notes to self: prioritize adding a small python helper to convert the above loadgen JSON -> YAML for the existing runner and ensure the seed is threaded into sampling RNGs and the runtime jitter suppression flags.
